title: Lock dimension skeleton for avatar and pill buttons to eliminate shift
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Avatar and pill-shaped icon buttons occasionally shift content when transitioning from icon to loading spinner or when an icon is swapped by runtime tooling. This is most visible in compact lists and the topbar, and becomes worse under theme inversion (dark mode) where spinner color swaps change perceived bounds. Several regression reports from QA and customers noted micro-layout shift and flicker during high-frequency state changes.

Proposed solution: introduce a lightweight 'size-lock' token and a minimal skeleton slot for compact avatar and pill buttons. Key elements: 1) enforce an explicit width/height baseline token (btn.compact.minWidth / btn.avatar.lockSize) applied when a button may show transient content; 2) provide a zero-margin internal skeleton element that replaces icon area without changing outer box-sizing; 3) deferred spinner fade-in (120ms threshold) to avoid flashing for sub-120ms ops; 4) theme-aware skeleton tint token so the skeleton doesn’t invert in dark mode causing perceived jump.

Design constraints and trade-offs: we prefer a minimal visual change (no new shapes or large skeletons) to avoid surprising product surfaces. Adding fixed minWidths increases potential truncation in very constrained layouts — mitigation: use tokenized breakpoints that increase truncation threshold only in compact variants. We rejected fully fluid width with CSS content-visibility because it introduced more repaint churn on older browsers.

Success metrics: reduce cumulative layout shift (CLS) on pages with >10 buttons by >= 70% in internal regression harness; reduce customer-reported layout-shift tickets for buttons to zero for new rollouts; no a11y regressions (tab order, focus ring preserved).

Notes for engineering: CSS-first approach with a small runtime guard for spinner delay. Provide a single opt-in flag on Button API (sizeLock: true) for surfaces where we don't want to change existing contracts by default. The design token values should be provided at theme token level (light/dark) and fall back to computed variable when missing.
acceptance_criteria: Compact avatar/pill buttons have stable bounding box during icon->loading and icon swaps
Spinner is shown only after 120ms by default and is customizable via prop/attribute
Theme-aware skeleton uses provided tokens and does not invert unexpectedly in dark mode
Unit and visual regression tests added; CLS regression harness shows >=70% improvement
Design review signoff and an accessible focus state preserved for keyboard users
accessibility_notes: Ensure skeleton element is aria-hidden and focusable element remains the native button. For icon-only buttons provide an offscreen label via aria-label. Verify color contrast of skeleton tint tokens against background in both light and dark themes.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge CSS token and API opt-in behind feature flag. 2) Ship to internal Canary customers and visual regression harness. 3) Monitor CLS and customer support for 2 weeks. 4) Flip opt-in default in a minor release if metrics hold. Rollback plan: revert feature flag and patch spinner delay to previous behavior.
